note: Leads are not verified parsers. Ranks are assigned only among verified paths.

leads.name: sqlparser
leads.reason: Parser::parse_sql(&GenericDialect, sql) returns Vec<Statement> AST.

leads.name: sqlparser_derive
leads.reason: Proc-macro helper for sqlparser's AST visitors; no parser.

leads.name: datafusion-sql
leads.reason: DataFusion SQL planner over sqlparser ASTs; shared sqlparser-rs family, no own parser.

leads.name: sqlformat
leads.reason: Formatter; tokens to text, no syntax tree.

leads.name: pg_query
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: pg_query::parse returns the libpg_query protobuf parse tree; both valid controls equal the oracle. Verified with a clang 23.1.3 build of the vendored libpg_query sharing one LLVM profile with the Rust binding, and AFL++ feedback from the Rust crates plus the gram.c, scan.c and parser.c objects (nm-checked).

leads.name: sqllogictest
leads.reason: Parser and runner for the sqllogictest script format; it does not parse SQL statements into a syntax tree.

leads.name: sqlite3-parser
leads.family: SQLite grammar (lemon-rs port of SQLite's Lemon parse.y)
leads.reason: Parser::new(&Bump, bytes) yields Cmd/Stmt AST values from the generated Lemon parser; both valid controls equal the oracle (string literals unquoted by the adapter). Verified with Rust source coverage of the crate and its generated parse.rs and whole-binary cargo-afl feedback.

leads.name: libsql-sqlite3-parser
leads.family: SQLite grammar (lemon-rs port of SQLite's Lemon parse.y)
leads.reason: Near-identical fork of an older sqlite3-parser release: 98.1% of its 13,501 source lines match sqlite3-parser 0.12.0 (difflib over 14 common .rs/.y files, 4 byte-identical), against 68.0% for the selected 0.17.0. Not a separate parser; the family is represented by sqlite3-parser.

leads.name: polyglot-sql
leads.reason: SQL transpiler with its own parser.

leads.name: gluesql-core
leads.reason: Database engine; parses through sqlparser-rs.

leads.name: fsqlite-parser
leads.reason: Cargo.toml license-file = LICENSE, an MIT text with a rider that withholds all rights from named parties and restricts use in evaluation harnesses; not an open-source license, so the path is ineligible. Not run.

leads.name: sqlparser-dsql
leads.reason: Fork of sqlparser 0.62.0 with Aurora DSQL extensions: 99.7% of sqlparser 0.62.0 source lines are retained and they make up 97.3% of the fork (44 common files, 26 byte-identical). Same parser as the selected sqlparser path.

leads.name: spacetimedb-sql-parser
leads.reason: Business Source License 1.1 (not open source until its change date) and it parses through sqlparser-rs.

leads.name: sql_query_builder
leads.reason: Query builder; emits SQL.

leads.name: databend-common-ast
leads.family: Databend SQL parser (logos tokenizer, nom/pratt combinators)
leads.reason: In the recorded 'sql parser' snapshot. tokenize_sql + parse_sql(Dialect::PostgreSQL) return Databend's own AST; both valid controls equal the oracle.

leads.name: sqlparser-lance
leads.reason: Its crates.io description calls it a fork of sqlparser-rs (0.32.0, 2023, repository field points at sqlparser-rs). Old fork of the selected sqlparser; overlap not measured.

leads.name: qusql-parse
leads.family: qusql-parse hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
leads.reason: Found in the recorded 'sql parser' search snapshot (3,272 recent downloads). parse_statements(sql, &mut Issues, &ParseOptions) returns typed statements; both valid controls equal the oracle with the default MariaDB dialect. Successor of sql-parse by the same author.

leads.name: typedpg_pg_query
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: Separate Rust binding over its own vendored libpg_query (MIT AND BSD-3-Clause AND PostgreSQL); shares only the generated protobuf module with pg_query (difflib: 33% of pg_query src lines). Not run in this round: it needs the same clang-23 dual-profile FFI build as pg_query. Next lead by metric.

leads.name: spg-sql
leads.family: spg-sql hand-written PostgreSQL-dialect lexer and recursive-descent parser
leads.reason: In the recorded 'sql parser' snapshot. parse_statement returns the SPG front-end AST; both valid controls equal the oracle.

leads.name: oxisqlite-sqlite3-parser
leads.family: SQLite grammar (lemon-rs port of SQLite's Lemon parse.y)
leads.reason: Another fork of the lemon-rs sqlite3-parser code (same description); overlap not measured in this round.

leads.name: proof-of-sql-parser
leads.family: Proof of SQL LALRPOP grammar over sqlparser-rs types
leads.reason: Cryptographic Open Software License 1.0 (not an OSI open-source license) and a restricted SQL subset for the Proof of SQL engine.

leads.name: sqlglot-rust
leads.reason: In the recorded 'sql parser' snapshot. parse_statements(sql, Dialect::Ansi) returns a typed AST; both valid controls equal the oracle.

leads.name: turso_sqlite3_parser
leads.family: SQLite grammar (lemon-rs port of SQLite's Lemon parse.y)
leads.reason: Fork of the lemon-rs sqlite3-parser code (same description and repository); overlap not measured in this round.

leads.name: nom-sql
leads.reason: parse_query_bytes returns a SqlQuery AST; both valid controls equal the oracle (decimal rebuilt from Real {integral, fractional}).

leads.name: sql-ast
leads.reason: README says it is forked from sqlparser-rs; 96.1% of sqlparser 0.5.0 source lines reappear (90.4% of sql-ast 0.8.0, 13 common files). Near-identical fork of an old release of the selected sqlparser.

leads.name: banshee_parser
leads.reason: Lossless CST parser; below the ten-path ceiling once nine paths are verified and not evaluated in this round.

leads.name: pgmold-sqlparser
leads.reason: Its description calls it a fork of sqlparser with extra PostgreSQL features; same parser family and release line as the selected sqlparser 0.64.0. Overlap not measured.

leads.name: sql-parse
leads.family: qusql-parse hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser (predecessor)
leads.reason: Predecessor name of qusql-parse: its repository README says the project moved to the qusql-parse folder of antialize/qusql, and 50.5% of sql-parse 0.28.0 source lines reappear in qusql-parse 0.12.0 (difflib over the 21 common file paths). Excluded as a predecessor name, as trust-dns-proto was for hickory-proto.
